conflicts.description: Which chase bulbs each Chase Light II group lights. The board's block diagram (printed 3-14) draws J4 (G.I. string 01, public G.I. 0, lamps 91-94) to A-16087 alone and J3 (string 04, G.I. 3, lamps 95-98) to A-16088 chained on to A-16089, and draws no bowl board. The factory parts list instead puts the strip socket A-16088 plugs into on A-16087, so A-16087 and A-16088 form the chained pair and A-16089 takes its own cable; it runs one ramp cable in the J4 colours (H-15871) and one in the J3 colours (H-16213, 'front chase lite cable') without saying which board each plugs into, and the bowl cable H-15870 in the J3 colours. The manual's cable list adds an H-16214 'Center Chase Light Cable' that neither assembly lists. No source gives the socket order of the four strings on any of the four boards, and the Power Driver Board connector list puts solenoids 20 and 24 on the opposite J2 pins from the chase board's page, which would swap strings 2 and 3 of each group. A recreation therefore cannot tell which ramp bulbs go dark with which address or which G.I. string switches which ramp section. Resolution path: on a machine, pull J3 and then J4 at the Chase Light II board and note which ramp and bowl bulbs go dark, then film the ramp and bowl while the T.15 RAMP LIGHTS TEST cycles (stopping it switches the chase power off) and note which bulbs go dark together and in which order, or with the ramp off check continuity from each board's header pins to its sockets; any owner of a working machine can do it in minutes.

End-of-stroke leaf switch of the lower flipper assembly. cftblGameData declares FLIP_SOL(FLIP_L), so PinMAME synthesizes this address from the flipper coil state after the stroke time and its public level is not a measurement of the contact; normally_closed records the Fliptronic grounded-switch convention (closed to ground only at end of stroke). The T.1 run showed the ROM naming the synthesized bit when it fired the flipper.

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball rolls onto the outhole switch 55 at the trough's outhole end; the outhole kicker (solenoid 12, A-8039-3) kicks it into the trough. The three balls rest on switches 58 (nearest the outhole), 57 and 56 (at the exit end), and the ball release coil (solenoid 4, B-9362-L-2) kicks the ball on 56 into the shooter lane, the others rolling down behind it.
mechanisms.label: Outhole and three-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: No solenoid drives the shooter lane: the player plunges the ball resting on switch 66 with the manual plunger, up past the P-A-I-D lanes (25-28).
mechanisms.label: Manual plunger shooter lane

mechanisms.behavior: A ball in the F-I-L-M hole breaks the beam of opto 34; the popper coil (solenoid 1, A-15769) kicks it back to the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Top right popper (F-I-L-M hole)

mechanisms.behavior: The left hole (switch 16, K-I-S-S) and the centre hole (switch 17, Snack Bar) drop the ball into a subway under the playfield that delivers it to the lower right popper, where it breaks opto 37; the popper coil (solenoid 3, A-15842) kicks it back to the playfield. In the subway run the ROM fired solenoid 3 for the ball the host delivered to 37 after either hole.
mechanisms.label: Left and centre holes, subway and lower right popper

positions.label: Ball in the lower right popper

mechanisms.behavior: The A-16042 Lift Ramp Assembly under the head of the left ramp carries an up coil (solenoid 23, SM1-2B-900-DC, a DC solenoid) and a down coil (solenoid 26, AE-26-1200), both with tieback diodes, and the position switch 38. Public 38 is 1 while the ramp is down: the retained script writes 1 when 26 fires and 0 when 23 fires, and pinned cftbl_handleMech sets it from the same commands. Pinned cftbl.c's simulator sends a ball entering the left ramp (switch 36) up the upper (Creature) ramp to switch 64 while 38 is 1 and along the swirl ramp past switch 62 otherwise; that routing is the simulator's, not a measured fact.
mechanisms.label: Lift ramp at the head of the left ramp

mechanisms.behavior: Three jet bumpers (A-9415-2 coils, SW-11A-37 skirt switches): the top left one fires solenoid 13 from switch 45, the top right one 14 from 46 and the bottom one 15 from 33.
mechanisms.label: Three jet bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Two kicking slingshots (SW-1A-114 switches): the left one (A-14369-L) fires solenoid 6 from switch 47 and the right one (A-14369-R) solenoid 5 from switch 48.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Four stand-up targets (A-16206-2): Cola (41) and Hot Dog (42) on the left, Popcorn (43) and Ice Cream (44) in the centre. Completing them opens the Snack Bar in the centre hole.
mechanisms.label: Snack Bar stand-up targets

mechanisms.behavior: The A-15993 bowl: the ball circles the whirlpool past its micro switch 65 and drops through the centre. The bowl flasher (solenoid 10) lights it, and the A-15672 board under it carries eight chase bulbs on the Sequential G.I. #2 group (see mechanism.sequential-gi-chase).
mechanisms.label: Whirlpool bowl

mechanisms.behavior: The Chase Light II board A-15541 under the playfield switches two G.I. strings onto eight chase strings: G.I. string 01 (public G.I. 0) onto LAMP 1A-4A on J4 and string 04 (public G.I. 3) onto LAMP 1B-4B on J3. Solenoids 20 and 24 select one of four codes on a 74LS139 whose two halves see the same bits; the selected string of each group goes dark and the other three stay lit, so the chase is a dark string stepping through each group. PinMAME publishes the selected (dark) string as lamps 91-98 (see those devices). The T.15 RAMP LIGHTS TEST cycles the codes 0, 1, 2, 3 and stopping it switches G.I. 0 and 3 off. The 32 #86 chase bulbs sit on three eight-lamp boards on the swirl ramp (A-16089, and A-16088 chained to A-16087) and on the bowl's A-15672; the bowl's cable carries the J3 group. Which ramp boards each group drives and which bulbs belong to which string are unresolved (conflict.chase-light-board-group-assignment).
mechanisms.label: Sequential G.I. chase lights

mechanisms.behavior: The hologram that makes the Creature appear in the playfield window: the hologram lamp (solenoid 28, #1156) and the mirror motor (solenoid 27, 48 VAC) sit in the cabinet bottom, and the push motor (solenoid 21, 48 VAC) under the playfield. The retained script shows its hologram image while 28 is on and animates it while 27 runs.
mechanisms.label: Creature hologram

mechanisms.behavior: Two Fliptronic flippers: lower right (FL-11629, A-15205-R-2; power 45, hold 46) and lower left (FL-15411, A-15205-L-4; power 47, hold 48). Each cabinet button breaks both optos of its Flipper Opto Switch Board (112 and 116 right, 114 and 118 left), and the ROM fires the flipper from either. PinMAME synthesizes the end-of-stroke bits 111 and 113 from the coil state.
mechanisms.label: Lower flipper pair

physical.notes: Chase string LAMP 1A of the Chase Light II board A-15541 (J4-3, Orange-Brown, triac Q4), powered by G.I. string 01 (public G.I. 0). Not a lamp-matrix position: cftblGameData declares lampCol = 1 and pinned wpc.c's WPC_CFTBL handling writes the public lamp matrix's ninth column, public 91-98, as 0x11 shifted by the decoder code (solenoid 20 plus twice solenoid 24), so this address and its partner in the other group are 1 while the code is 0, whatever the G.I. does; only PinMAME's separate physical-output (modulated lamp) path ANDs the selection with the G.I. triacs. The selected code is the output the 74LS139 pulls low, and on the board the low output turns its string off while the other three conduct (Chase Light II Schematic, printed 3-15). So this address is 1 while string 1A is the dark one: the string's bulbs are lit while G.I. 0 is on and public 91 is 0. The T.15 RAMP LIGHTS TEST cycles 91, 92, 93, 94 in order, each of 95-98 with its partner, and stopping it switches G.I. 0 and 3 off while PinMAME keeps publishing the selected pair. The retained VPW script lights its chase phase while the address is 1 and its G.I. is on, one phase lit and three dark, the inverse of the board. The ramp's and the bowl's 32 #86 chase bulbs are on three eight-lamp boards on the swirl ramp and one in the bowl; which bulbs belong to this string, and which ramp boards this group drives, are unresolved (conflict.chase-light-board-group-assignment), so the device has no placement and no quantity.
